skill.name: extension-authorization
skill.description: Adds Internet Identity authentication and role-based access control patterns for Caffeine AI apps using the caffeineai-authorization package.
skill.summary: Guide for Caffeine AI authentication, RBAC guards, user profiles, and verified email attributes.
skill.author: caffeinelabs

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, relative imports, and identity terminology. Semantic review found a high-risk first-admin bootstrap pattern because the first authenticated user becomes admin without a token or preconfigured owner. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: First authenticated user becomes administrator without proof of ownership.
remediation.suggestion: Require a deployer-controlled owner principal, one-time setup secret, or explicit setup step before assigning the first admin role.

remediation.issue: Public access before admin bootstrap can create an account takeover window.
remediation.suggestion: Document a safe deployment sequence and block privileged endpoints until the intended owner completes setup.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated First-Admin Bootstrap
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that the first authenticated user automatically becomes admin and no token or secret is required. A public deployment could be taken over by any early user before the intended owner logs in.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The same bootstrap behavior is documented twice with no secret, token, or fixed owner principal. The risk depends on deployment timing, but the takeover path is clear.

content.user_title: Add Role-Based Authorization to Caffeine AI Apps
content.value_statement: Caffeine AI apps need reliable identity, profile, and role checks before exposing private data. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured authorization pattern for backend and frontend work.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to include MixinAuthorization and AccessControl in a Caffeine AI backend.
Provides Motoko guard patterns for admin-only and user-only endpoints.
Defines profile methods for caller profiles and admin profile lookup.
Explains verified Internet Identity name and email capture during sign-in.
Provides frontend login, logout, session restore, and profile loading patterns.
Includes migration guidance for moving authorization projects to version 1.0.0.
limitations: It targets Caffeine AI projects that use Motoko and Internet Identity.
It depends on caffeineai-authorization and core-infrastructure packages already being available.
It does not provide a full custom authentication system.
It requires careful owner bootstrap planning before public deployment.

use_cases.title: Add Access Control to a New App
use_cases.description: Use the skill to add standard authentication, authorization state, and role checks to a new Caffeine AI project.

use_cases.title: Protect Backend Methods
use_cases.description: Use the guard patterns to restrict data reads, data writes, and role assignment methods in Motoko canisters.

use_cases.title: Build Login and Profile Flows
use_cases.description: Use the frontend patterns to manage login state, restored sessions, user profiles, and logout cache clearing.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Authorization
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Caffeine AI app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the extension-authorization pattern to my Caffeine AI app. Include backend setup, role state, login flow, and a simple protected user profile.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Existing Methods
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate update for an existing backend.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing Motoko public methods and apply the right authorization guards for admin, user, owner, and guest access.

prompt_templates.title: Build Authenticated UI Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Frontend implementation with session restore handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a frontend login and profile setup flow that handles restored sessions, logout cache clearing, and unauthorized access screens.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate and Capture Verified Email
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration with Internet Identity attributes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Migrate my project to caffeineai-authorization 1.0.0 and add verified Internet Identity email capture through MixinAuthorization.

output_examples.input: Add authorization to a new private notes app.
output_examples.output: A backend setup plan, protected profile flow, role guard checklist, and frontend login states for private notes access.

output_examples.input: Restrict admin features and personal profile access.
output_examples.output: A permission mapping that separates admin actions, owner-only profile access, authenticated user actions, and guest screens.

output_examples.input: Migrate my authorization package and collect verified email.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist covering package versions, mixin argument updates, frontend dependency updates, and verified email storage.

best_practices: Define the intended first admin before public deployment.
Gate every sensitive backend method with a role or ownership check.
Clear cached application data when the user logs out.
anti_patterns: Do not gate authenticated UI on login success alone.
Do not store unverified email attributes as trusted identity data.
Do not leave sensitive public methods available to guest principals.

faq.question: What type of projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for Caffeine AI apps that use Motoko, Internet Identity, and role-based access control.

faq.question: Does it replace Internet Identity?
faq.answer: No. It builds authorization patterns around Internet Identity and Caffeine AI infrastructure.

faq.question: Can it support admin-only screens?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes backend admin guards and frontend access denied handling.

faq.question: Can it read verified email attributes?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents how MixinAuthorization can capture verified name and email values during sign-in.

faq.question: Does it handle custom username and password login?
faq.answer: No. The skill says custom authentication requires removing the authorization package and replacing the checks.

faq.question: What should authors review before publishing?
faq.answer: They should review first-admin bootstrap controls, protected endpoint coverage, and logout cache clearing.
